title: One Point Lesson - Vibration Trend Monitoring & Alarm Response (VSHH-1201) (OPL-GA-1201A-07)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-GA-1201A-07 - Vibration Trend Monitoring & Alarm Response (VSHH-1201).

Equipment: GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP), Discipline: Instrument, Area: 1200 – HEXANE FEED SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-1201 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-1201.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
Vibration trend monitoring & alarm response (VSHH-1201) for GA-1201A (HEXANE FEED PUMP) in the HEXANE FEED SYSTEM.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 – Action: Record VT-1201 on the daily PdM route in mm/s RMS
- Step 1 – Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 – Action: Note alarm at 4.5 mm/s and trip at 7.1 mm/s (VSHH-1201)
- Step 2 – Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 – Action: A rise greater than 1 mm/s within a week = plan a bearing inspection
- Step 3 – Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 – Action: Correlate the vibration rise with TI-1201 bearing temperature
- Step 4 – Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 – Action: Escalate to reliability engineer if the 1x running-speed component dominates
- Step 5 – Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Scheduled proof test of low-low suction pressure trip — set-point drift found +0.08 barg | Likely Cause: Switch set-point drift found +0.08 barg during proof test | Action: Recalibrated PSLL-1201 to 0.5 barg trip, function tested to DCS
- Symptom: PDI-1201 reading erratic, seal-flush low alarm nuisance-tripping | Likely Cause: Impulse lines fouled with hexane residue/polymer fines | Action: Cleaned impulse lines and re-zeroed PDI-1201 transmitter
- Symptom: Discharge flow control hunting, FIC-1201 oscillating | Likely Cause: Loop poorly tuned after transmitter re-range | Action: Re-ranged FT-1201 and retuned FIC-1201 PID parameters

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A rising vibration trend predicts bearing failure days in advance and lets you plan a repair before a trip.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-1201: PSLL-1201 trips at < 0.5 barg – never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-1201 before working on GA-1201A.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
